correctness.rationale: Nonzero-distinct n edge outputs exhaust all \(2^m-1\) nonzero masks, giving \(2^{m-1}\) positive edges per coordinate. Each selected item covers two edges, hence each pool >=\(2^{m-2}\), equality iff pool independent. Explicit item integer masks i for even i, 1 for \(i\equiv1\pmod4\), 0 for \(i\equiv3\pmod4\) produce blocks of OR outputs (4r+1,4r+3,4r+2,4r+4), final cyclic output n-1. Each bit pool has exactly \(2^{m-2}\) pairwise nonadjacent items. Complete all-m proof and verifier runs for m=2..13 from the packaged verify.py; finite checks are not extrapolated as proof.

originality.rationale: The exact number m of tests for cycles is not claimed new: Bousquet et al. (arXiv:1605.02588) already optimize the union-distinguishing palette for most cycles with nonempty edge labels. The new precise objective is total item-to-pool incidence under a related but weaker empty-or-exactly-adjacent-pair model, with a sharp \(m2^{m-2}\) lower bound, equality structure, and uniform balanced construction. Their accessible full text presents the cycle minimum palette, not this incidence objective. Müller–Jimbo 2CPD has stronger individual-column disjointness; balanced constant-weight Gray-code constructions use restrictions incompatible with our variable-weight masks. Plausible inaccessible older/conference sources and unindexed results remain a risk; this is not an independence certification.

value.rationale: The quantity minimized is the physical count of sample uses in a cyclic nonadaptive pooled screening experiment at information-theoretically full outcome capacity. It simultaneously minimizes per-test pool size and achieves exact perfect balance. The infinite family, forced equality structure and explicit closed-form construction provide a natural exact resource benchmark beyond the previously studied minimum number of tests, while limited to a specific defect model and noiseless assays.
